ai.definition: AI Agentic Workflows involve AI systems that can plan, execute, and critique their own actions within a task environment. These workflows are recursive in nature, allowing the AI to iteratively improve its performance on complex tasks through self-assessment.
ai.howItWorks: The system employs ReAct (Reason + Act) prompting techniques, where it reasons about the current state and then acts by calling appropriate APIs or tools to perform specific actions. After each action, the AI reflects on the outcome and adjusts its strategy accordingly.
ai.problemSolved: Automating multi-step tasks in complex environments that require decision-making, tool usage, and iterative improvement without human intervention.
ai.manufacturing: The manufacturing process is primarily software-based, involving development of algorithms, training datasets, and integration with existing tools and APIs.
ai.buildProcess: Developers create the AI models using machine learning frameworks, train them on relevant data, and integrate these models into workflows that can interact with various software environments through API calls. Continuous testing and refinement are necessary to ensure robust performance.
ai.costDrivers: Costs include development of AI models, training data acquisition, integration with third-party tools, and ongoing maintenance and updates.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: Expected to grow as more enterprises seek automation solutions for complex tasks.
ai.regulation: Current regulatory landscape is unclear; potential need for guidelines on AI transparency, accountability, and data privacy in enterprise settings.
ai.risks: Potential risks include over-reliance on flawed AI models, security vulnerabilities in API integrations, and ethical concerns related to decision-making autonomy.
ai.profitability: High potential for profitability as adoption increases; requires careful cost management and value proposition demonstration to enterprises.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development may focus on enhancing explainability, improving cross-domain adaptability, and expanding the range of applicable tasks.
ai.energyRequirements: Field units draw low hundreds of watts; fabrication is energy-intensive due to computational requirements but can be optimized with cloud-based solutions.

glossary.def: A method where AI systems reason about a task and then act by calling appropriate APIs or tools, followed by reflection on the outcome.
Autonomous processes where AI plans, executes, and critiques its own actions to solve complex tasks iteratively.

subsystems.name: Reasoning model
subsystems.role: the language model that reads the task, reasons step by step and decides what to do next.

subsystems.name: Orchestration loop
subsystems.role: runs the plan–act–observe cycle, tracks state and decides when the task is done.

subsystems.name: Tool layer
subsystems.role: lets the agent affect the outside world: call APIs, run code, search, send messages.

subsystems.name: Memory and retrieval
subsystems.role: remembers past steps and brings in relevant documents or history.

subsystems.name: Critic and verifier
subsystems.role: checks the agent's own output for errors, contradictions or policy violations.

subsystems.name: Observability and guardrails
subsystems.role: records what the agent did, limits its permissions and controls cost and risk.

buildSteps.title: Define the task and success criteria
buildSteps.detail: Write down exactly what the agent must achieve, what tools it may use and how success will be measured before any prompt is written.

buildSteps.title: Choose and configure the model
buildSteps.detail: Select a foundation model with strong reasoning and tool-calling ability, then set temperature and context limits for the task.

buildSteps.title: Build the tool interface
buildSteps.detail: Wrap each external action as a typed function with a clear description so the model can call it correctly.

buildSteps.title: Implement the orchestration loop
buildSteps.detail: Code the plan–act–observe cycle: the model proposes an action, the system executes it, feeds back the result and repeats until a stopping condition is met.

buildSteps.title: Add memory and retrieval
buildSteps.detail: Store intermediate steps in a scratchpad and connect a vector database so the agent can recall facts or documents beyond its context window.

buildSteps.title: Insert a critic step
buildSteps.detail: After each major output, run a separate check — either a second model call or deterministic rules — to catch mistakes before they propagate.

buildSteps.title: Test against a benchmark set
buildSteps.detail: Run the agent on representative tasks, measure success rate, cost and latency, then iterate on prompts, tools and loop logic.

buildSteps.title: Deploy with guardrails
buildSteps.detail: Restrict permissions, set spending caps, log every action and keep a human able to pause or take over.

pathway.milestone: single-agent copilots for coding, research and customer support
pathway.unlocks: productivity gains in narrow, well-defined tasks with human oversight.

pathway.milestone: multi-agent systems with specialised roles and shared memory
pathway.unlocks: end-to-end automation of multi-step business processes.

pathway.milestone: reliable long-horizon autonomy with robust self-critique
pathway.unlocks: delegation of complex projects that run for hours or days.
